note: constant A B b is x ↦ b. Thus the constant function computes judgmentally, as in the book.

J.ny defines inverse by transport of refl x in the family z ↦ (z = x), not by an induction rule. The book's defining clause symm(refl a) ≡ refl a holds only as the identification inverse_refl (module 04). This is by design of HOTT: HOTT has no regularity, so transport along refl is not definitionally the identity.

concat p q (J.ny) is the book's p ∙ q, which the book writes as q·p. It transports p along q in the family y ↦ (x = y). The book's defining clause trans(p)(refl b) ≡ p holds only as the identification concat_p1 (J.ny). This is by design of HOTT: HOTT has no regularity, so transport along refl is not definitionally the identity.

The formalization has all six items, with the printed orientations. J.ny gives concat_p1 (p ∙ refl = p) and concat_1p (refl ∙ p = p). Module 04 gives concat_assoc, concat_inverse_left (p⁻¹ ∙ p = refl b), concat_inverse_right (p ∙ p⁻¹ = refl a) and inverse_inverse. Neither unit law is judgmental in HOTT. The formalization proves concat_assoc and the inverse laws by J from the unit laws and inverse_refl.

transport (J.ny) is native transport refl B p .trr. The book's defining clause trp_refl ≡ id holds only as the identification transport_refl (module 04). This is by design of HOTT: without regularity, transport along refl in a variable family is not definitionally the identity.

The formal statement is an identification of functions trp(p ∙ q) = trp(q) ∘ trp(p), that is, the book's trp(e′∘e) = trp(e′) ∘ trp(e). It follows by function extensionality from the pointwise transport_concat. The proof of transport_concat uses J on q.

The formal statement is an identification of functions trp[B](p) = id_B for the constant family. It follows by function extensionality. Transport along any p in a constant family is judgmentally transport along refl in B. Thus the pointwise identification is transport_refl. This identification is not judgmental, because HOTT has no regularity.
map_path f p is native refl f p. The book's defining clause ap_f(refl x) ≡ refl f(x) holds judgmentally (the proof of ap_refl is refl).

The formalization has all three parts: ap_f(p ∙ p′) = ap_f(p) ∙ ap_f(p′), ap_f(p⁻¹) = ap_f(p)⁻¹ and ap_id(p) = p. The first part is the book's ap_f(p′·p) = ap_f(p′)·ap_f(p). The proofs of the first two parts use J, with concat_p1 and inverse_refl in the reflexive case. The reason is that refl ∙ refl ≡ refl is definitional in the book's argument, but not in HOTT. ap_identity holds judgmentally (refl).
The two functions have the printed type. The identification trp[T∘f](p) = trp[T](ap_f(p)) holds judgmentally: native transport in T∘f along p is transport in T along refl f p (proved by refl).
happly p is x ↦ p (refl x), that is, the native application of a path of functions to refl x. The book's clause ptw(refl f) ≡ (x ↦ refl f(x)) holds judgmentally.

naturality h p : ap_f(p) ∙ h(x′) = h(x) ∙ ap_g(p) is in concat order. It is the book's h(x′)·ap_f(p) = ap_g(p)·h(x). The definition uses J on p. The value at refl is concat_1p followed by the inverse of concat_p1. The book needs only the first step, because p ∙ refl ≡ p holds by definition in the book. The definition reaches this value only up to the typal Jβ, by design of HOTT.

section_raw: Identifying elements in members of families of types}
note: PathOver is Narya's native heterogeneous identity type Id B p u v, not a family defined by path induction. Over refl x it is judgmentally Id (B x) u v, which is the book's defining clause. The universe U of the statement has no role (the formalization uses native Type).

section_raw: Identifying elements in members of families of types}
note: Over a constant family Z, the type of paths over p is judgmentally z = z′: pathover_constant_type is refl. pathover_constant_equiv is the identity equivalence. The book gets the identification by induction on p.

section_raw: Identifying elements in members of families of types}
note: pathover_transport_type constructs po_p : (y =_p y′) = (trp_p(y) = y′) for every family as a path in the universe, by J on p. The induced equivalence is pathover_transport_equiv. The book's clause po_refl ≡ refl is not even well-typed here, because trp_refl(y) ≢ y. HOTT has no regularity, so for a variable family, transport along refl is not definitionally the identity. Also, Jβ is typal. The formalization replaces the clause by pathover_transport_refl: at refl, the map sends refl y to transport_refl y. This determines po by path induction. pathover_of_eq (module 00) is the direct inverse direction.

section_raw: Identifying elements in members of families of types}
note: pathover_concat q q′ is the second component of the concatenation (p, q) ∙ (p′, q′) in Σ X Y. It lies over concat p p′ = p′∘p. Likewise, pathover_inverse is the second component of the inverse in Σ X Y. (pathover_inverse is the inverse that is defined after the block.) The book's defining clause says that the composite is q when p′ and q′ are reflexive. This clause holds only as pathover_concat_refl_right_strong (module 281), a path from the composite to q over concat_p1. The inverse of refl is refl only up to pathover_inverse_refl_strong, over inverse_refl. Both are typal by design of HOTT (concat p refl ≢ p).

section_raw: Identifying elements in members of families of types}
note: This is an open-ended exercise. The formalization states the six groupoid laws for pathover_concat and pathover_inverse (module 17) in two forms. In module 281 (suffix _strong), each law is a path over the corresponding law in the base, in the family t ↦ (u =_t v). The base laws are concat_p1, concat_1p, concat_inverse_right, concat_inverse_left, inverse_inverse and concat_assoc. This is the book's 'modification'. For example, the law compares q⁻¹∘q and refl v over concat_inverse_left A x y p. The cylinder transport that defines concat_p1 proves the right unit law. The other laws are proved by J on the base path and on the path over it. In the reflexive case, the proof transports along the typal Jβ (by design of HOTT). In module 150 (the same names without suffix), each law is the .snd of the law in Σ A B. Thus it lies over its .fst, a base 2-path that depends on q. An identification of that .fst with the law in A fails with Narya bug E0500. Narya raises this error when it compares the .fst of, for example, concat_p1 (Σ A B) … with another term. A check of the projection against its own type succeeds. The strong forms never form 2-dimensional Σ-paths.

section_raw: Identifying elements in members of families of types}
note: apd f p is native refl f p : Id Y p (f x) (f x′). The book's defining clause apd_f(refl x) ≡ refl f(x) holds judgmentally.

note: apap g p q is native refl g p q, for a path q over p. The computation at (refl x, refl y) is judgmental (apap_refl is refl).

section_raw: Identifying elements in members of families of types}
note: apap g (refl x) q = ap_{g(x)}(q) holds judgmentally (apap_refl_left is refl). The book proves it by induction on q.
The formalization defines Product A B as Σ A (_ ↦ B), the sum over a constant family, as in the remark.

The formal content of the notation is as follows. The triple (x,y,z) is (x,(y,z)) in the iterated sum. For a family over pairs, the reassociation equivalence sigma_assoc identifies ((x,y),z) with (x,(y,z)). Its map sends one to the other judgmentally (triple_reassociation is refl). The n-fold notation needs no further statement.

BookIsContr A is Σ(c:A) Π(x:A) (c = x), the book's definition, with contraction paths from the center. Native isContr (univalence.ny) uses the opposite orientation x = c. book_contraction and native_contraction convert between them.
The formal statement is BookIsContr (Σ(x:X) (a = x)) for all a : X. book_contraction gets it from the native contractibility of based path spaces (iscontr_idfrom, univalence.ny).
BookFiber f y is Σ(x:X) (y = f x), the book's orientation. The native Fiber (module 00) uses f x = y. The two are equivalent (fiber_conventions_equiv).

BookIsEquiv f is Π(y:Y) BookIsContr (BookFiber f y), literally the book's definition. Native isEquiv (module 00) uses the opposite orientations of fibers and contractions. book_equivalence and native_equivalence (module 11) convert between the two notions and keep the map.

BookEquiv X Y is the record (map : X → Y, equiv : BookIsEquiv map), that is, Σ(f : X → Y) isEq(f). Native Equiv has the same shape with native isEquiv. The types are equivalent (equivalence_conventions_equiv, module 20).

The map of canonical_inverse_equiv e : Equiv Y X is equiv_inverse_map e, that is, y ↦ fst(fst(t y)), the book's f⁻¹. The function (X ≃ Y) → (Y ≃ X) is stated for native Equiv. book_equivalence converts it to BookEquiv and keeps the map. native_equivalence keeps .center .fst. Thus the inverse is the same.
compose_equiv e d : Equiv X Z has the map x ↦ d(e(x)), for native Equiv. book_equivalence converts it to BookEquiv and keeps the map.

The formalization has all three cases. Here e : h∘f = g is an identification of functions A → C, and the types are arbitrary. The cases are stated for the book's BookIsEquiv (book_two_out_of_three_*) and also for native isEquiv (two_out_of_three_*).

Forward direction: for an equivalence e, g = equiv_inverse_map e satisfies g(f(x)) = x (equiv_retraction) and f(g(y)) = y (equiv_counit). Converse: book_quasi_inverse_equiv f g η ε is a BookEquiv whose map is f. Its construction uses quasi_inverse_equiv (module 08). quasi_inverse_equiv adjointifies through the indexed Martin-Löf identity type eq of src/internal/ml-paths.ny, which is loaded in HOTT mode (see Trust in README).

The formal statement is for an arbitrary path-dependent family B(x,i). The map is the book's f, with a definition by J (contract_away_map). The inverse is b ↦ (a, refl a, b). The book's defining clause f(a, refl a, b) ≡ b holds only as contract_away_beta, an instance of the typal Jβ (J.ny). This is by design of HOTT. contract_away_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of the book's f explicitly.

The formal statement is the instance of contract_away_equiv for a B that does not depend on i. Thus the map is the same f with a definition by J. Also, f(a, refl a, b) = b holds only up to contract_away_beta (typal Jβ, by design). contract_away_simple_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of the same f for a B that does not depend on i.

The formal statement is Σ(x:X) B(x) ≃ Σ(y:Y) B(f⁻¹(y)), with f⁻¹ = equiv_inverse_map, the book's canonical inverse. The construction pulls back along f⁻¹ (sigma_pullback_equiv, through ua) and then inverts. sigma_pullback_equiv_map (module 289) identifies the map of sigma_pullback_equiv X Y e P with (x, c) ↦ (e x, c).

The formalization proves the more general form Π(x:X) Π(i : a = x) B(x,i) ≃ B(a, refl a). The printed case is the judgmental specialization B(x,i) ≔ B(x). The map is evaluation at (a, refl a), and the inverse is J. One inverse law uses the typal Jβ.
totalize f is (x, y) ↦ (x, f(x)(y)), literally tot(f).

family_equiv takes the family of equivalences f(x) : Y(x) ≃ Z(x). It returns an equivalence Σ Y ≃ Σ Z whose map is judgmentally totalize (x ↦ f(x) .map). Its inverse is the totalization of the inverses, as in the proof. family_equiv_book_map (module 289) gives the book's form. Let f : Π x (B x → C x) satisfy BookIsEquiv (f x) for all x. Then BookIsEquiv (Σ A B) (Σ A C) (totalize A B C f).

The details of the proof of lem:fiberwise are the body of family_equiv. This body gives the inverse tot(x ↦ f(x)⁻¹) and both inverse laws, pointwise by equiv_retraction and equiv_counit. Then it applies quasi_inverse_equiv.

If tot(f) is an equivalence, then every f(x) is an equivalence (native isEquiv). The book fiber of tot(f) over (x, z) is equivalent to the book fiber of f(x) over z (total_fiber_equiv, through contract_away_equiv). Contractibility transfers along that equivalence.

The formalization proves this statement and does not postulate it. happly (the book's ptw) is an equivalence of dependent functions, with inverse funext and both inverse laws (funext_eta, funext_beta_function). The formalization states it as a native Equiv and as a BookEquiv whose map is happly by construction. funext uses J and Narya's native action of paths on function types (x ⤇ …). Its law happly(funext h) = h rests on the typal Jβ (funext_beta). No funext axiom is involved. function_extensionality_book_map (module 289) directly states BookIsEquiv (f = g) (Homotopy f g) (happly A B f g). Here happly A B f g is the book's ptw.
The formal statement is (Unit → X) ≃ X as a native Equiv, with the map f ↦ f(star).
The formal statement is (Σ(x:X) Unit) ≃ X as a native Equiv. Its map is the first projection.
The formal statement is (X × Σ(y:Y) Z(y)) ≃ Σ(y:Y) (X × Z(y)) as a native Equiv, with the printed factor order.
The formal statement is (Σ(x:X) Σ(y:Y) Z(x,y)) ≃ Σ(y:Y) Σ(x:X) Z(x,y) as a native Equiv. The map swaps the components.

For every z, (gf)⁻¹(z) is equivalent to CompositeFiberSplit = Σ(w : g⁻¹(z)) f⁻¹(fst w), with book fibers z = g(y) and y = f(x). Both inverse laws are explicit (composite_fiber_from_to, composite_fiber_to_from). singleton_to_ind is the singleton induction that the proof uses. This is different from composite_double_fiber_equiv in module 104.
The formal statement is (Π(x:X) Σ(y:Y) Z(x,y)) ≃ Σ(f : X → Y) Π(x:X) Z(x, f x) as a native Equiv. The statement is more general: Y can depend on x. The printed case takes a constant family.

The formal statement is (Π(z:Z) Y(f z)) ≃ SectionAbove = Σ(g : Z → Σ(x:X) Y(x)) (f = fst ∘ g) for arbitrary types. Its map is judgmentally s ↦ (z ↦ (f z, s z), refl f). section_above_equiv_map records this.

The formal statement is the currying equivalence ((Σ(x:X) Y(x)) → C) ≃ Π(x:X) (Y(x) → C) as a native Equiv. The statement is more general: the codomain can depend on (x, y). The printed case takes a constant codomain Z.
pair x y is (x, y). pair_path p q is literally apap pair p q, as printed. It coincides judgmentally with the native Σ-path sigma_path_pair (p, q) (pair_path_sigma is refl).
pair=(refl x, q) = ap_{pair(x)}(q) holds judgmentally (pair_path_refl_left is refl). The book proves it by induction on q.

sigma_path_equiv is a native Equiv, for arbitrary u, v : Σ X Y. Its map is pair= (sigma_path_pair, which is judgmentally equal to pair_path). The formalization also records the subsequent identifications fst(pair=(p,q)) = p, snd(pair=(p,q)) = q (through apd) and r = pair=(fst r, snd r). These are pair_path_fst, pair_path_snd and pair_path_eta. All three are judgmental for native Id. sigma_path_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of (p, q) ↦ pair_path … p q (pair= = apap pair).

The map is exactly (p, q) ↦ pair=(p, q) (product_pair_path), with q read as a path over p in the constant family. The formalization proves that this map is an equivalence, both as native Equiv (product_path_equiv) and as BookIsEquiv of that map.
The formal statement is (Π(b:Bool) T(b)) ≃ X × Y as a native Equiv, with the map f ↦ (f(false), f(true)). Here T(false) = X and T(true) = Y (BoolFamily). The universe hypothesis has no role.
The formal statement is X × Y ≃ Y × X as a native Equiv. The map swaps the components.
The map e(f) = f(star) is a BookIsEquiv (true_universal_property). The underlying native equivalence is unit_evaluation_equiv.
The formal statement is X + Y ≃ Σ(b:Bool) T(b) as a native Equiv, with the map inl x ↦ (false, x), inr y ↦ (true, y).

The formal statement is (x = y) ≃ SumCode x y for all four constructor combinations, without set assumptions. SumCode computes to a = a′ for inl/inl, to b = b′ for inr/inr and to Empty for the mixed cases. The encode-decode proof uses higher-dimensional matching on Sum, not transport.

Precomposition with inl and inr (sum_restrict) is an equivalence (X + Y → Z) ≃ (X → Z) × (Y → Z) for arbitrary types. The formalization states it as native Equiv (sum_universal_property) and as BookIsEquiv of that map. Its inverse is sum_elim.
The formal statement is (X + Empty) ≃ X as a native Equiv. The map sends inl x to x.

NegNat is a wrapped copy of Nat with constructor minus. The destructor negnat_value computes judgmentally on constructors (-(-n) ≡ n, negnat_value_minus is refl). The formalization proves -(-m) = m by induction on m (negnat_minus_value). Both the constructor and the destructor are equivalences.
List A is the native inductive type with constructors nil (ε) and cons. Functions that are defined by match on it compute judgmentally on constructors, as the book's induction principle states.

If A is contractible (native isContr, which is equivalent to the book's notion), then length : List A → Nat is an equivalence. The underlying map of length_equiv is the actual length function, with inverse n ↦ repeat c n (length_repeat, repeat_length). length_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv (List A) Nat (length A) for contractible A.
append concatenates two lists by recursion on the first argument, as the book hints. reverse uses append.
The formal statement is ℓ1(ℓ2ℓ3) = (ℓ1ℓ2)ℓ3 in the book's orientation. The proof uses induction on ℓ1 (as the inverse of append_assoc).

The map of transport_equiv p : Equiv X Y is exactly native transport p .trr in the identity family (= transport Type (T ↦ T) p). Its equivalence proof comes from id_to_equiv, which is defined by J. The two are identified (id_to_equiv_transport, id_transport_equiv_path). The book's clause trp[id_U](refl X) ≡ id_X holds only as transport_refl, by design of HOTT (no regularity). The universe is the single native Type.

The formalization proves this statement for the single native Type and does not postulate it. ua comes from the vendored univalence.ny and is built with glue. It satisfies both inverse laws (ua_beta, ua_eta). transport_univalence_equiv (native Equiv) and book_univalence (BookEquiv, with book fibers and contractions) are equivalences. By construction, their map is exactly p ↦ ptoe(p) = p .trr, but their types do not name the map. The formalization also proves the subsequent identifications etop(id) = refl (ua_identity) and etop(g f) = etop(f) ∙ etop(g) (ua_compose, the book's ḡ·f̄). For a universe U of the model (modules 190–193), (X =_U Y) ≃ (X ≃ Y) is universe_path_equiv. Its map is id_to_equiv ∘ fst, with id_to_equiv based on J. This map is homotopic to transport by id_to_equiv_transport. Module 289 names the map in the types: transport_univalence_equiv_book_map and book_univalence_book_map state BookIsEquiv of ptoe = trp[id_U], into Equiv A B and into BookEquiv A B.

The formal statement is (Bool = Bool) ≃ Bool. The map sends refl to false (bool_loops_equiv_refl) and swap = ua(bool_not) to true (bool_loops_equiv_swap). Every loop is equal to the representative of its image (bool_loop_classification). Also, swap ≠ refl (bool_swap_nontrivial), and the proof of this uses the transport computation of ua. Finally, swap · swap = refl (bool_swap_squared).
FunctionFamily Y Z is x ↦ (Y(x) → Z(x)), literally the book's family.

The formal statement is trp[Y→Z](e)(f)(y′) = trp[Z](e)(f(trp[Y](e⁻¹)(y′))), with a proof by J on e. The book argues that at refl all transports are identities by definition. This argument does not apply in HOTT (no regularity). Thus the reflexive case uses transport_refl and inverse_refl explicitly. The special case after the construction is trp[X ↦ (X → X)](ua g)(f) = g ∘ f ∘ g⁻¹. The formalization proves it as an identification of functions (transport_endomorphism_ua, with transport_inverse_ua). Native companions (module 284) hold by refl. With the backward transport .trl along e in place of transport along e⁻¹, the lemma holds definitionally (transport_function_family_trl). ua(g).trl is the inverse map of g (ua_trl). Transport of an endomorphism along ua(g) is g ∘ f ∘ g⁻¹ as functions (transport_endomorphism_ua_trl).

The formal statement is trp(e)(i) = ap_g(e) · i · ap_f(e)⁻¹, with a proof by J on e. The formalization reads the unbracketed composite as concat (ap_f e)⁻¹ (concat i (ap_g e)). That is ap_g(e)·(i·ap_f(e)⁻¹) up to concat_assoc. The reflexive case uses transport_refl, concat_p1, concat_1p and inverse_refl (typal by design of HOTT).

The formalization has all four cases, with the printed orientations. They are transport_constant_path (i), transport_path_from (e·i, that is, i ∙ e), transport_path_to (i·e⁻¹, that is, e⁻¹ ∙ i) and transport_conjugation (e·i·e⁻¹). trp-in-a=x holds judgmentally, because native concat is this transport. trp-in-x=a and conjugation are instances of transport_path_family. The first case is transport_refl in a constant family.

The formal statement is trp(e)(i) = po_e(apd_g(e)) · ap_{trp(e)}(i) · po_e(apd_f(e))⁻¹. Here po_e is the map of pathover_transport_equiv (def:pathover-trp), applied to apd (pathover_transport_section). The brackets are as in lem:trp-in-fx=Ygx. The proof uses J on e. The base case uses the typal computation of po at refl (pathover_transport_refl) and the naturality of transport_refl. Both are necessary because Jβ and transport along refl are typal by design of HOTT.

The formal statement is Equiv (f(x) =_p f(x′)) (f(x) = f(x)). Its definition uses J on p, with the identity equivalence in the reflexive case. The formalization reads the printed e in the path-over type as p. It copies the printed right-hand side literally. The value of this equivalence at refl is the identity equivalence only up to the typal Jβ, by design of HOTT.
trp[h ↦ (y = h(x))](e)(p) = ptw(e)(x)·p (concat p (happly e x)) holds judgmentally for native Id (pointwise_transport is refl). The book defines it by induction on e.

The formalization has the negation of a proposition, equations a = b between elements of a set, and a ≠ b. It packages each of them as an element of PropTypes (Σ(P:Type) isProp P), together with its proof that it is a proposition. Prop is the global PropTypes, not Prop_U of a model universe.
Every proposition is a set, for an arbitrary type.
bool_set has type Π(a b : Bool) isProp (a = b), which is isSet Bool unfolded. Its proof uses encode-decode on Bool, not the printed argument of Simon Huber.

The formalization has all six numbered clauses: empty_prop and unit_prop (1), pi_prop (3), product_prop (4), sigma_prop (5) and decidability_prop (6, P + ¬P). Clause 2 (A → P) is the constant-family instance of pi_prop, as the book remarks. It has no separate declaration. negation_prop is the subsequent remark that A → ∅ is a proposition.

The formalization has all four clauses, for every h-level: hlevel_function (1), hlevel_pi (2), hlevel_product (3) and hlevel_sigma (4). HLevel uses index 0 for contractible types, 1 for propositions and 2 for sets. Thus a book n-type is HLevel (n+2), and the clauses cover every n ≥ −2.

isProp, isSet and isGroupoid (module 00) are literally the three displayed definitions. The inventory lists only isSet. General n-types are HLevel (n+2) (module 15), whose base case is contractibility.
The formalization has all five items: BookIsContr (book_iscontr_isprop), isProp, isSet, isGroupoid and, for the general n-type clause, HLevel k for every k. hlevel_isprop covers book n = k − 2.
isProp, isSet, isGroupoid and isEq are propositions. For isEq, this holds both for the book's BookIsEquiv (book_isequiv_isprop) and for native isEquiv (isequiv_isprop).
The formalization has both implications. They are stated with native isContr, whose contraction goes towards the center. book_contraction converts to the book's orientation.

The formal content of the remark is as follows. A filler of a square of functions is an identification g∘p = q∘f (SquareFiller). A filler of a square of identifications is an identification g·p = q·f of the composite paths (PathSquareFiller). Fillers of the first kind form a proposition when the sink is a set (square_filler_prop). Fillers of the second kind form a proposition when the relevant identity type is a set (path_square_filler_prop). The informal notion of a diagram as a graph is not formalized.

The formalization constructs the truncation and does not postulate it. The construction is the impredicative encoding Mere T ≔ Π(P : Type) isProp P → (T → P) → P. It quantifies over the single universe, so it relies on Type : Type. (The pinned Narya has neither HITs nor universe levels.) In a stratified theory, this corresponds to propositional resizing. Mere T has the element constructor mere, and it is a proposition (mere_isprop). It has the induction principle into families of propositions (mere_eliminate). Together these inhabit TruncationSignature (native_truncation), and the chapter's truncation results are stated for TruncationSignature. The nondependent computation rule holds judgmentally (mere_rec_beta is refl). The dependent rule f(|t|) ≡ g(t) holds only as the identification mere_eliminate_beta, because the pinned Narya has no higher inductive types. The universal property after the definition is mere_universal_property_book_map: precomposition with |–| is a BookIsEquiv (Mere T → P) → (T → P) for every proposition P. In the universe model (modules 190–193), closure under truncation is the field trunc_small of a Universe. This matches the book's postulate of the HIT in each universe. Thus ‖T‖ is essentially U-small whenever T is (mere_essentially_small).

IsNonEmpty T A is T .carrier A for an arbitrary TruncationSignature. NonEmpty A is its instance at native_truncation, that is, Mere A. The formalization proves the footnote ¬(T = ∅) ≃ ¬¬T for arbitrary T (not_empty_double_negation). The proof uses ua for ¬T → (T = ∅) (negation_empty_path).

Or T P Q is T .carrier (P + Q) for an arbitrary TruncationSignature. Disjunction P Q is its instance at native_truncation (disjunction_native_or is refl). That is, Disjunction P Q is Mere (P + Q), packaged as an element of PropTypes.

Exists T X P is T .carrier (Σ(x:X) P x) for an arbitrary TruncationSignature. Existence X P is its instance at native_truncation (existence_native_exists is refl). That is, Existence X P is Mere (Σ(x:X) P x), packaged as an element of PropTypes.

ExistsUnique X P is BookIsContr (Σ(x:X) P x), with the book's contraction orientation. UniqueExistence packages it with its proof that it is a proposition (book_iscontr_isprop). No truncation is used.

The formal statement is Mere (Σ(t:T) (x = |t|)) for x : Mere T. The proof is for the constructed truncation and uses recursion into that proposition. The identification x = |t| comes from mere_isprop. The proof chooses no representative.

A proposition P is equivalent to its truncation. The map is |–|, and the inverse is the recursor applied to the identity. trunc_prop_equiv states this for an arbitrary TruncationSignature, and mere_proposition_equiv states it for native_truncation.

For an arbitrary TruncationSignature, the formalization defines Component T A a ≔ Σ(x:A) ‖a = x‖. It also defines IsConnected T A ≔ ‖A‖ × Π(x y : A) ‖x = y‖. NativeComponent and Connected are the instances at native_truncation. connected_isprop (module 43) states that isconn(A) is a proposition. It is not in the declaration list.

The formalization has both parts, for an arbitrary TruncationSignature, with native instances (native_component_connected, native_same_component_properties). First, the component of a is connected. Second, for P : A → PropTypes and ‖x = y‖, P(x) = P(y) as an identification in PropTypes.
A connected set is contractible, with the book's contraction orientation (BookIsContr), for an arbitrary TruncationSignature. The native instance is native_connected_set_contractible.

If every a = a is a proposition, then A is a set (loops_prop_set). If such an A is also connected, then it is contractible (BookIsContr), for an arbitrary TruncationSignature. The native instance is native_connected_loops_prop_contractible.
Σ(x:A) B(x) is connected when A and every B(x) are connected, for an arbitrary TruncationSignature. The native instance is native_connected_sigma.

This is a remark about terminology. To merely construct an element of T means to construct an element of its truncation. This truncation is S .carrier T for a TruncationSignature S, concretely Mere T (native_truncation, module 29).

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: IsSurjection T f ≔ Π(b:B) ‖BookFiber f b‖, for an arbitrary TruncationSignature. That is, every book fiber b = f(a) is merely inhabited. Surjective is the instance at native_truncation. The footnote is formalized: split surjections Π(b:B) Σ(a:A) (b = f a) are equivalent to sections g : B → A with f∘g = id_B (split_surjection_section_equiv). The map of this equivalence is split_surjection_to_section by refl. section_to_split_surjection is the explicit converse map.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The book's injection is IsEmbedding f ≔ Π(b:B) isProp (BookFiber f b), literally isinj(f). PathReflecting (module 02) is a different, weaker notion: path reflection Π(a a′ : A) (f a = f a′) → (a = a′). This notion agrees with injectivity only for set codomains (xca:inj-sets).

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The formalization has maps in both directions between isinj(f) (IsEmbedding, propositional book fibers) and path reflection (PathReflecting). The first direction holds for arbitrary A and B. The second direction uses isSet B, as printed. The constant function Unit → SetTypes with value (Bool, bool_set) is boolean_set_point. The formalization proves that it is not injective. Injectivity would make the loops of Bool in SetTypes a proposition, and this contradicts the nontriviality of bool_swap.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The formalization has both directions, for an arbitrary TruncationSignature with native instances. It uses the book's fiber and contraction orientations. If an injection f is a surjection, then f itself is a BookIsEquiv (embedding_surjection_equiv_book_map). embedding_surjection_equiv packages it as a BookEquiv with map f. Conversely, an equivalence is an injection and a surjection (book_isequiv_embedding, book_isequiv_surjection). embedding_surjection_iff packages the iff as an equivalence of propositions.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: Let A be non-empty and let B be connected. Then every injection f is a BookIsEquiv (nonempty_connected_embedding_equiv_book_map). The proof goes through the surjectivity of f (nonempty_to_connected_surjective). Only the nonemptiness of A is necessary, as in the book. The statement is for an arbitrary TruncationSignature with native instances.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The codomain of a surjection from a connected type is connected. The formalization proves both nonemptiness and pairwise mere paths. The statement is for an arbitrary TruncationSignature with a native instance.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The formal statement is (z = z′) ≃ ap_f⁻¹(snd(z′)·snd(z)⁻¹) for book fibers z, z′ : f⁻¹(b). It has the printed fiber direction and difference path (concat (snd z)⁻¹ (snd z′)). The proof follows the book's chain: paths over the base path (pathover_mapped_paths_type) and the rearrangement of path equations (path_difference_equiv).

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The formalization has both directions, without set assumptions. If f is an injection, then each ap_f = map_path f is a BookIsEquiv (embedding_on_paths_book_map). embedding_on_paths packages it as a BookEquiv with that map. The converse is path_equivalences_embedding. The footnote warning is formalized. When B is a set, all ap_f are equivalences iff f reflects paths (only B needs to be a set). path_reflection_not_sufficient refutes the general implication through boolean_set_point : Unit → SetTypes.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The formalization has all four clauses, and each clause is an iff. HLevel k represents book level k − 2. Clause (1) is fibers_hlevel_to_ap and ap_hlevel_to_fibers, without conditions. For clause (2), the if direction is loop_fibers_to_fibers, and the only-if direction is the instance fibers_hlevel_to_ap … a a. For clause (3), the if direction is connected_map_equiv_from_paths_book_map: f itself is a BookIsEquiv. The only-if direction is map_equiv_to_paths, which needs no connectedness. For clause (4), the if direction is connected_map_equiv_from_loops_book_map, and the only-if direction is the instance map_equiv_to_paths … a a. connected_equivalence_loop_criterion (module 93) states (4) as one equivalence of propositions. The connected clauses are stated for an arbitrary TruncationSignature, with native instances.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: Let f : A ≃ B and g : Π(a:A) F(a) ≃ G(f a). Then the formalization gives an equivalence Σ A F ≃ Σ B G (native Equiv). It is the composite of the fiberwise equivalence and the pullback along f (sigma_pullback_equiv, through ua). The universe U of the statement has no role.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: Image f ≔ Σ(b:B) Mere (BookFiber f b) is the printed formula with the book's fiber orientation. It uses the constructed propositional truncation.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The formalization gives the canonical factorization f = i∘p through the image, with a surjective p and an injective i. The triangle commutes judgmentally (image_triangle is refl, as the footnote says). The full six-component type ImageFactorizations is contractible for arbitrary A and B, with the canonical factorization as center. C ranges over the single native Type, not over a universe U. Contractibility concerns the whole 6-tuple, which includes the given triangle. For fixed C, g, h, the formalization does not claim that the type of triangles is contractible. The unnumbered diamond property that follows in circle.tex (3076–3096, eqn:image-univ-prop) is also proved (image_universal_property). It states that diagonal equivalences with both triangles and their two-dimensional compatibility form a contractible type. The proof uses no set assumption and no surjection cancellation into arbitrary targets.

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: If the codomain B is a set, then the image is a set (image_set takes isSet B).

section_raw: More on equivalences; surjections and injections}
note: The formalization has both directions, as an equivalence of propositions. One direction is restriction along the canonical map to the image. Its inverse is truncation recursion into the proposition-valued family (image_prop_eliminate).

section_raw: Decidability, excluded middle and propositional resizing}
note: Decidable A ≔ A + ¬A is defined for any type A. The book's notion is its instance for a proposition. decidability_prop shows that it is then a proposition.

section_raw: Decidability, excluded middle and propositional resizing}
note: ExcludedMiddle ≔ Π(P : Type) isProp P → P + ¬P is a type, and excluded_middle_prop proves that it is a proposition. The formalization introduces no inhabitant or axiom. Results that use LEM take it as an explicit hypothesis. ExcludedMiddle quantifies over all propositions of the single Type. LEM for the propositions of a model universe U is LEMFor U (module 192).

section_raw: Decidability, excluded middle and propositional resizing}
note: LEM is equivalent to isEquiv of the exact map b ↦ (true = b) : Bool → PropTypes (truth_proposition). The statement uses this exact map, not only the existence of some equivalence Bool ≃ PropTypes. The two directions are excluded_middle_truth_equiv and truth_equiv_implies_excluded_middle. Prop is the global PropTypes. The version for a model universe (LEMFor U with Prop_U) is not stated.

section_raw: Decidability, excluded middle and propositional resizing}
note: The formalization has both implications between LEM and double-negation elimination for all propositions. dne_implies_excluded_middle is the requested implication. The two implications are packaged as an equivalence of the two principle types. Neither principle is assumed globally.

section_raw: Decidability, excluded middle and propositional resizing}
note: The formal content is as follows. LEM implies LPO (excluded_middle_implies_lpo), and every instance of LPO is not refutable (double_negated_lpo_instance). The claim that LPO is strictly weaker is a metatheoretic independence claim, and it is not formalized. The footnote is historical.

section_raw: Decidability, excluded middle and propositional resizing}
note: Narya has a single Type : Type. Thus a proposition-valued predicate small on Type models a univalent universe U (Universe, module 190). This predicate is closed under Empty, Unit, Bool, Nat, binary sums, Σ, Π, identity types and the propositional truncation. A nested pair U : U′ adds cumulativity and small_U′(U). The principle is stated literally, for every nested pair, as BookIsEquiv of the map P ↦ P : Prop_U → Prop_U′ (prop_inclusion). That map is always an embedding (prop_inclusion_embedding). The formalization proves that the principle is equivalent to 'every U′-proposition is essentially U-small' (resizing_equiv). The principle is used only as a hypothesis. The universe of all types (total_universe) is the only concrete instance. The formalization makes no consistency claim.

section_raw: Decidability, excluded middle and propositional resizing}
note: For every nested pair U : U′, excluded middle for the propositions of U′ (LEMFor U′) implies propositional resizing. The reason is that a decided proposition is equivalent to Unit or Empty, and both of these lie in U (decided_prop_essentially_small). The global ExcludedMiddle of module 70 is derived as a special case (excluded_middle_resizing).

Let U be a universe of the model (module 190). Then EssentiallySmall U A ≔ Σ(X : U) (A ≃ X), with native Equiv. The formalization proves that it is equivalent to the book-convention version (essentially_small_book_equiv). LocallySmall U A requires all identity types to be essentially small. The formalization proves the following remarks. Essential smallness is a proposition by univalence (essentially_small_prop). Small types are essentially small. Essentially small types are locally small. The criterion through a reflexive U-valued relation Eq_A is proved in both directions (locally_small_from_relation, locally_small_relation). The formalization takes the induced map as the transport of the reflexivity witness (relation_paths_map). The map defined by path induction agrees with it up to an identification (typal Jβ). In the model, the smallness predicate is replete. Thus a type is essentially U-small exactly when it lies in U (essentially_small_is_small). The book's distinction between the two disappears.

U is locally U-small: (X = Y) ≃ (X ≃ Y) by univalence (universe_path_equiv), and X ≃ Y lies in U. The formalization proves closure properties for every universe of the model. Essentially small types are closed under Π over a U-small base, Σ, products, sums, truncation and equivalence types. Locally small types are closed under Π over a U-small base (the printed example, pi_locally_small), Σ, products, subtypes, identity types and equivalences.

Resizing for U : U′ is equivalent to the statement that every U′-proposition is essentially U-small (resizing_equiv). An arbitrary model universe U, together with the universe of all types, models the book's U₀. The statement that every proposition is essentially U-small is PropsEssentiallySmall U. It is equivalent to resizing from U into the universe of all types. It also implies resizing for every nested pair with lower universe U. Under this assumption, every set is locally U-small.

The principle is stated literally for a universe U of the model, as a proposition (replacement_prop). As in the book, it is used only as a hypothesis. The formalization does not derive it: the book's join-construction proof needs pushouts, and the pinned Narya has no pushouts (no higher inductive types). It holds trivially in the universe of all types (total_replacement). The formalization makes no consistency claim. The comparison with set-theoretic replacement is informal and not formalized.

Replacement implies that the component A_(a) = Σ(x:A) ‖a = x‖ of a locally U-small type is essentially U-small. The reason is that it is the image of the constant map Unit → A at a (component_image_equiv). The following sentence is also proved. Under replacement, the type FinSet of finite sets is equivalent to the image of Fin : ℕ → U (fin_image_finite_sets). Thus FinSet is essentially U-small (finite_sets_essentially_small).

A predicate on T is a map T → PropTypes (Subtypes T). Here Prop is the global PropTypes = Σ(X : Type) isProp X. Predicates valued in Prop_U for a universe of the model are PropU-valued maps (module 191). DecidablePredicate T pairs a predicate with a decision P(t) + ¬P(t) for every t.

Part 1 reads yes as true. bool_true_decidable gives Decidable (b = true) for every b. Thus f(t) = true is a decidable predicate on an arbitrary T (it is a proposition by bool_set). bool_value_predicate packages it as a DecidablePredicate T. But the type of bool_value_predicate does not mention f. Thus the body, not the type, states the claim. Part 2: every decidable proposition P satisfies (P ≃ Unit) + (P ≃ Empty), with native Equiv.
Sub(T) is literally Subtypes T ≔ T → PropTypes. T_P is literally SubtypeCarrier T P ≔ Σ(t:T) P(t). Prop is the global PropTypes over the single native Type.

For any proposition-valued family P, ((x₁,p₁) = (x₂,p₂)) ≃ (x₁ = x₂). The map is the first component of the native Σ-path, that is, ap_fst. subtype_path_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of ap_fst explicitly.

The formal justification of the convention has two parts. First, paths in the subtype are paths in T (subtype_path_equiv). Second, over a point where the predicate holds, the book fiber of the projection is contractible (subtype_point_fiber_contractible). The notational coercion itself is not a formal statement.

The formalization defines Prop_U and Set_U for every universe U of the model (PropU, SetU). It shows that they are subtypes of U: the projection is an embedding (prop_u_subtype, set_u_subtype). For every nested pair U : U′, both lie in U′ (prop_u_in_upper, set_u_in_upper). The global PropTypes and SetTypes are equivalent to the instances PropU and SetU for the universe of all types. They are not literally equal to them.
PropTypes is a set, and Sub(T) is a set for every T (the sentence after the lemma). This is stated for the global PropTypes. For every model universe U, Prop_U is also a set (prop_u_set, module 284).

For arbitrary X, T, f and P, the displayed type Σ(g : X → T_P) (f = fst∘g) is equivalent to Π(x:X) P(f x) (subtype_factorization_equiv). The proof uses function extensionality, type-theoretic choice and projection fibers. The formalization gives the iff as an equivalence between Π(x:X) P(f x) and the book contractibility of the displayed type.

InjectionsInto T ≔ Σ(S : Type) Σ(f : S → T) Π(t:T) isProp (BookFiber f t). This is exactly the nested Σ of Inj^U(T) with the book's isinj. S ranges over the single native Type, not over a chosen universe U.

The formal statement is Sub(T) ≃ Inj(T) for every T. The map sends P to (T_P, fst, _), and the inverse sends (S, i) to t ↦ i⁻¹(t), both judgmentally. The formalization supplies both inverse laws (subtypes_injections_eta, subtypes_injections_beta). The second law uses the equivalence between maps and families (lem:typefamiliesandfibrations), that is, ua. subtypes_injections_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of P ↦ (T_P, fst, _) in full.

The formalization gives the proof of lem:Sub(T)=Inj(T) with both round trips. subtypes_injections_eta uses function extensionality and proposition extensionality on the projection fibers, as the book hints. subtypes_injections_beta uses maps_families_eta, that is, ua. It does not use the hinted argument with the map g of the footnote.
For every book n ≥ −1: if T has HLevel (n+2) and P is proposition-valued, then T_P has HLevel (n+2).

The formalization has all partial-order laws on the set Sub(T): inclusion_refl, inclusion_trans and inclusion_antisym, with inclusion a proposition. It also has both bounds (empty_subtype_least, full_subtype_greatest). The construction works for arbitrary T, not only for sets. Antisymmetry gives equality in Sub(T), not equality of the carriers.

DecidableSet A ≔ Π(x y : A) isProp (x = y) × Decidable (x = y). The definition is itself a proposition (decidable_set_prop), and it implies that A is a set (decidable_set_is_set). The formalization proves the following remark that every proposition is a decidable set (proposition_decidable_set). The contrast with decidability as a proposition needs no statement.

The formal statement is Hedberg's theorem for an arbitrary type with decidable equality. Its conclusion is the book's DecidableSet, which includes that identity types are propositions. The proof uses weakly constant endomaps of identity types (collapsible_paths_set) and explicit path algebra. It assumes no set hypothesis.

Pointed is the type of pointed types Σ(A : Type) A, a record with carrier and point. A₊ is plus_pointed (A + Unit, inr star). BookPointedMap is the type of pointed maps in the book's orientation pt_Y = f(pt_X). This type is judgmentally the fiber of evaluation at the base point. The composition is book_pointed_compose (g÷f÷, g÷(f_pt)·g_pt). PointedMap (module 00) uses the opposite orientation f(pt_X) = pt_Y. pointed_map_conventions_equiv compares it with the book's notion.
book_pointed_identity X is (id_A, refl a) in the book-oriented type of pointed maps (module 98).

This is only a notational convention. The coercions that it allows are the projections X .carrier of a pointed type and f .fst of a pointed map. Here f .snd is the pointing path in the book orientation pt_Y = f(pt_X). The printed f_pt : pt_X = f(pt_Y) is a typo in the book, and the formalization reads it in this orientation. book_pointed_to_native converts to the native orientation of PointedMap.

A₊ = (A + Unit, inr star). The formal statement is (A → B÷) ≃ (A₊ →* B) with book pointing paths. The map is plus_extend (extension by the base point, pointed by refl). One inverse law holds by reflexivity. The other law follows from the pointed-map path characterization (plus_extend_restrict). The book names no map. plus_forget_adjunction_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of plus_extend (extension by the base point).
The formal statement is Σ(b:B) (A →* (B,b)) ≃ (A÷ → B). Its map is judgmentally the forgetful map (b, f) ↦ f÷ (pointed_map_chosen_target_map is refl).
The definition is a pointed map with book pointing paths, together with BookIsEquiv of the underlying map.

Let r : X = Y. The carrier component of r is r .carrier : X÷ = Y÷. def:pathover-trp converts the point component of r to q : pt_Y = r.carrier.trr(pt_X) (pointed_path_point). These two components give the displayed map to pointed equivalences (pointed_path_to_equiv). This map uses the transport map of r .carrier as ptoe. The formalization proves fiberwise that it is an equivalence: both total spaces over Y are contractible. The second total space is contractible by book univalence and singleton contraction. pointed_path_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of the book's map explicitly.

The formal statement is (f = g) ≃ Σ h, (h(pt_X)·f_pt = g_pt), with book pointing paths and composition order. The proof follows the book's chain: Σ-paths, the path over as transport in T(k) = (pt_Y = k(pt_X)) (def:pathover-trp), and base change along function extensionality. The analogue of step (*) is judgmental here, because transport in T along e is ptw(e)(pt_X)·f_pt by definition (xca:trp-in-y=_(x)). Step (**) is not necessary, because the base change is along happly itself and not along its inverse. The map of pointed_map_path_equiv is not the book's ptw_* by definition, because the reindexing sigma_pullback_equiv is defined by J on ua. The formalization identifies it pointwise with the explicit ptw_* (pointed_map_path_equiv_ptw, through sigma_pullback_equiv_map and sigma_transport_equiv_map). pointed_map_path_equiv_book_map (module 289) transfers the equivalence to this map.

The definition of ptw_* uses J on f = g and sends refl to (x ↦ refl, concat_p1 f_pt). The definition reaches this value only up to the typal Jβ, by design of HOTT. The formalization also proves that ptw_* is an equivalence (pointed_map_path_homotopy_equiv), through contractible total spaces.

The formalization has both numbered clauses, for equivalences and for identifications in the universe. If Y is a proposition, then X ≃ Y and X = Y are propositions (equivalences_prop, proposition_type_paths_prop). If Y is a set, then X ≃ Y and X = Y are sets (equivalences_set, set_type_paths_set). Only Y needs to be a proposition or a set. Thus PropTypes is a set (propositions_set), and SetTypes is a groupoid (sets_groupoid). These are stated for the global PropTypes and SetTypes over the single native Type. For every model universe U, Set_U is also a groupoid (set_u_groupoid). Identifications in Set_U are identifications of the underlying types (set_u_path_equiv). Both are in module 284.

Empty, Unit, Bool, ℕ, binary sums, the wrapped types Copy and lists are sets when their constituents are sets. The declarations are empty_set, unit_set, bool_set, nat_set, sum_set, copy_set and list_set. That section only anticipates general finite types Fin n. The formalization shows later that they are sets (fin_set). The proofs use encode–decode codes (for Bool, ℕ, sums and lists), not the printed argument. The footnote is formalized: the list identity equivalences (list_path_equiv, with ListCode) and the preservation of n-types for n ≥ 0 (list_hlevel).
If X and Y are sets, then X + Y is a set, by encode–decode (SumCode, xca:binary-sum-id).

The formalization constructs SetTrunc A and does not postulate it. SetTrunc A is the quotient of A by the mere-path relation ‖x = y‖ (rem:set-trunc-as-quotient), that is, the image of A → (A → PropTypes). It has the element constructor, and it is a set. It has the path characterization (|x|₀ = |y|₀) ≃ ‖x = y‖ (the footnote). It has the universal property with precomposition as the map and the uniqueness of the recursor (set_trunc_rec_eta). It also has dependent induction into families of sets. The nondependent computation rule holds judgmentally (set_trunc_rec_beta is refl). The dependent rule f(|t|₀) ≡ g(t) holds only as the identification set_trunc_induction_beta, because the pinned Narya has no higher inductive types. Size: under replacement, SetTrunc A is essentially U-small for A : U (set_trunc_essentially_small). def:join-construction-of-truncation formalizes the footnote on general n-truncations. Its level Trunc 1 A is the image of A → (A → NTypes 0), with propositions encoded as HLevel 1, not as isProp. Trunc 1 A is equivalent to SetTrunc A, compatibly with the units up to identification (trunc_one_set_trunc_equiv, trunc_one_unit_compare). Chapter 3 uses SetTrunc, whose recursor computes judgmentally.

A_(z) is TruncatedComponent A z ≔ Σ(a:A) z(a). At |a|₀ it is judgmentally NativeComponent A a (truncated_component_at_point is refl). The decomposition A ≃ Σ(z : ‖A‖₀) A_(z) has the actual map a ↦ (|a|₀, (a, |refl a|)). A is connected iff ‖A‖₀ is contractible, as an equivalence of propositions.
The formalization has the definition of weak constancy. It also proves that weak constancy is a proposition when the codomain is a set (the following sentence).

The formalization constructs g : Mere A → B through the proposition-valued image of f (weakly_constant_image_prop), as in the proof. The rule g(|x|) ≡ f(x) holds judgmentally (weakly_constant_rec_beta is refl), because the recursor of the impredicative Mere computes on |x|.

Quotient A R is the image of R : A → (A → PropTypes), exactly as printed, with [a] = (R(a), |(a, refl)|). It is a set, and [–] is surjective. With the single native Type : Type, the image is itself in Type. But the book's A/R lies one universe higher, and this is the reason for the size footnote. The size footnote is formalized in the universe model. For A : U and R with U-small values, A/R is equivalent to the image of R : A → (A → Prop_U) (quotient_small_image_equiv). Thus A/R is essentially U-small by replacement (quotient_essentially_small), because A → Prop_U is locally U-small. Alternatively, propositional resizing pushes the values of R into the lower universe (resized_relation).
The formal statement is (P = [a]) ≃ P(a) for every P : A/R and a : A, as an equivalence of propositions. The two directions are quotient_member_of_path and quotient_path_of_member.

The formalization has both clauses. The first clause is ([x] = [x′]) ≃ R(x, x′) (quotient_effective). The second clause is the contractibility of the full type of lifts Σ(g : A/R → B) (f = g∘[–]), for a set B and a compatible f. It uses the book contraction orientation, with center quotient_rec. The recursor computes judgmentally on classes (quotient_rec_beta is refl), as the book's f̄([x]) ≡ f(x) does.
The formal statement is an equivalence from the quotient by the constant Unit relation to Mere A (direction A/R → ‖A‖). Both types are propositions.

The formalization uses the exact cross-sum relation w₁ + d₂ = w₂ + d₁ on ℕ × ℕ. It uses the printed normal-form predicate (d = 0) ∨ (w = 0 ∧ d ≠ 0), with the truncated disjunction. The map is signed normalization, a BookEquiv. The formalization proves f([(w,d)]) = (w,d,p) for every element of Z, including the proof component. It also compares the quotient with the integers ℤ of chapter 3 (integer_quotient_equiv).

Narya efafad2 has no higher inductive types, so the HIT is not postulated. The constructed image quotient of def:quotient-set has all three constructors: sethood quotient_set, classes quotient_class and relation paths quotient_encode. It also has the displayed dependent induction into families of sets, with the boundary condition QuotientBoundary. The computation rule f([x]) ≡ b_x holds only as the identification quotient_induction_beta, because HITs are not available. The HIT is also given as the signature QuotientSignature (module 163), and this quotient inhabits it.

Narya efafad2 has no higher inductive types. Thus the formalization gives def:quotient-as-HIT as the record QuotientSignature. This record is a set with the class map, relation paths and dependent induction into families of sets. Its computation rule is an identification. The image quotient inhabits it (image_quotient_signature). Every inhabitant is equivalent to the image quotient, with both inverse laws (quotient_signature_equiv). This is the requested equivalence, for a class of types that is slightly larger than the book's HIT (typal β).

The formalization constructs the set truncation as the quotient by the relation ‖x = y‖ (mere_path_relation). It has the path characterization (set_trunc_paths), and its recursion principle computes judgmentally (set_trunc_rec). The footnote is formalized. Under replacement, the 0-truncation of A : U is essentially U-small (set_trunc_essentially_small). This 0-truncation is the image of the (−1)-truncated identity relation. Recursively, the (n+1)-truncation is judgmentally the image of the n-truncated identity relation (trunc_succ_image, def:join-construction-of-truncation). It is essentially U-small by replacement (trunc_essentially_small, trunc_small).

The induced relation is exactly a ≡_f a′ ≔ ‖f(a) = f(a′)‖. The type of equivalences e : A/≡_f ≃ ‖im(f)‖₀ with ‖–‖₀∘p = e∘[–] is contractible (induced_quotient_unique). This gives existence, the triangle and uniqueness. The chosen equivalence (induced_quotient_equiv) uses the book convention and has both inverse laws. Its triangle commutes judgmentally.

BookLe m n ≔ Σ(k:ℕ) (k + m = n), and BookLt m n adds k ≠ 0. These are the printed difference-witness definitions. The formalization proves the uniqueness of the difference (difference_unique) and the propositionality of both relations. It also compares both relations with the recursive order Le/Lt of module 07 (le_book_equiv, lt_book_equiv).

The formalization has the listed algebra and order properties. It proves (suc m = suc n) ≃ (m = n). The operations + and · are commutative and associative, and both distributive laws hold. The relations ≤ and < are transitive, and + preserves them on both sides. Also, · preserves ≤ on both sides. Further, (m ≤ n) ≃ (m < n) + (m = n) and (m ≤ n) × (n ≤ m) ≃ (m = n). Finally, ¬((m < n) × (n < m)). The order statements use the book's difference-witness relations. The parenthetical consequences are stated for the book relations (lt_irrefl is for the recursive order). The relation < is irreflexive (book_lt_irrefl, the case m = n of book_lt_asym). The relation ≤ is reflexive (book_le_refl, difference witness 0).
All three relations are decidable. Here ≤ and < are the book's difference-witness relations.

min(P) is least_number. For a proposition-valued P, decidability and Mere (Σ n, P n) give Σ n, P_min(n). Here P_min(n) = P(n) × Π m, P(m) → n ≤ m in the book's BookLe (IsMinimum), exactly eqn:min. The bounded search μ_P (bounded_min, through bounded_search) follows the printed first-hit algorithm and computes on 0 and successors. The formalization proves all displayed invariants (bounded_min_bound, _found, _minimal, _no_hit). P(n) → P_min(μ_P(n+1)) is minimum_from_witness. Its first component is judgmentally μ_P(n+1), although its type does not mention μ_P. The minimum type is a proposition (minimum_prop). Thus the truncated witness is eliminated into it.

The book has a notational convention that suppresses decidability witnesses. The formalization always uses them explicitly. The bounded search of def:Nwellordered decides P with the given decision procedure. The pigeonhole proof (lem:PHP) decides equality on Fin (suc n) (fin_decidable_equality). It uses the total order on ℕ to order the two witnesses.

Let N be given, and let f : ℕ → ℕ satisfy f(n) < N for all n < N+1 (BoundedNatMap). Then the formalization constructs actual witnesses m < n < N+1 with f(n) = f(m) (BoundedCollision). It uses BookLt. The proof is different from the printed bounded-search substitution argument. It transfers to maps Fin (N+1) → Fin N and finds a collision by recursion on N (fin_pigeonhole). The recursion removes the last input and its image.
If m < n (BookLt), then (Σ k, k < m) ≠ (Σ k, k < n) as types, literally. The proof uses the earlier invariance of cardinality of Fin and the comparison with bounded naturals.

For m > 0 (BookLt 0 m), the type of pairs (q, r) with r < m and n = q·m + r is contractible (euclidean_division_unique). This gives existence and uniqueness together. nat_quotient and nat_remainder project it. The construction is structural recursion on the dividend with remainder rollover, not the printed least-number construction. The formalization also proves the extension to integer dividends (integer_euclidean_division_unique). This extension is used at circle.tex:2434 and in the root construction. The quotient is an integer, and the remainder is a natural number strictly below the positive divisor. For negative dividends, the proof divides the constructor index and takes the complementary remainder. Uniqueness holds for all sign combinations.
Fin 0 = Empty and Fin (suc n) = Fin n + Unit, by recursion, as printed. fin_below_equiv fixes the names 0, …, n−1 of the elements. It sends inr star to 0 and inl to the successor.

The formalization has clauses 2–4. It has Fin 1 ≃ Unit (fin_one_equiv) and Fin 2 ≃ Bool (fin_two_equiv). It has Fin n ≃ Σ(k:ℕ) k < n for all n, with the book's BookLt (fin_book_below_equiv). It also has (Fin m = Fin n) → m = n (fin_path_cardinality), by recursive deletion of an element. Clause 1 (the list of the elements) has no declaration. For the record, Fin 0 has no elements, and Fin 1 has inr star. Fin 2 has inl (inr star) and inr star. Only the inverse laws of fin_one_equiv and fin_two_equiv witness that these lists are exhaustive.

IsFinite X ≔ Mere (Σ(n:ℕ) (X = Fin n)), with identifications in the universe, as printed. It uses the constructed propositional truncation. Thus it is a proposition. finite_sethood shows that every finite type is a set.

The formalization has both clauses, for every type X. Σ(n:ℕ) ‖X = Fin n‖ is a proposition (cardinality_witness_prop). It is equivalent to IsFinite X (finite_witness_equiv). The truncations are eliminated only into propositions.

The formalization has FinSet = Σ(S : Set) isfinset(S) and FinSet_n = Σ(S : Set) ‖Fin n = S‖, with identifications in the universe. It has Card from lem:maxonefinitetype, as printed. FinSet is a groupoid, and FinSet ≃ Σ_n FinSet_n (finite_sets_components). The book's identification follows by ua. The footnote is formalized literally. With identifications in Set, the book's FinSet_n is by definition the component Set_(Fin n). This is BookFiniteSetsAt, and the proof is reflexivity. Paths in the universe identify it with the components FinSet_(Fin n) and U_(Fin n). FiniteSetsAt uses identifications in U and is equivalent. The subsequent identifications FinSet_0 = FinSet_1 = Fin 1 and FinSet = im(Fin) are formalized. The closing remark is formalized: FinSet is equivalent to the image of Fin : ℕ → U. Under replacement, FinSet is essentially U-small for every universe U of the model. This uses that ℕ lies in U.

Every merely finite type has decidable equality (finite_decidable_equality) and is a set (finite_sethood). Together these give the book's decidable set. The proof first shows sethood. Then it eliminates the truncated finiteness witness into the proposition of decidable equality. It chooses no enumeration.

The formalization has all four parts, with FinSet_2 = TwoSets = FiniteSetsAt 2 and identifications in the universe with the printed orientations. First, T = T is a 2-element set (two_loops_two_element). Second, ¬Π_T (T = Fin 2) (two_sets_no_global_identification). Its proof uses the swap loop in bundled TwoSets. Third, Π_T ((T = T) = Fin 2) (two_sets_loops_identification). Fourth, Π_T (T = (Fin 2 = T)) (two_sets_points_paths_identification). The last part uses that evaluation at false is an equivalence from equivalences Bool ≃ T to T (two_pointed_enumeration). The proof of this is by elimination into a proposition. No global enumeration is assumed.

The actual lookup map List X → Σ(n:ℕ) (Fin n → X) is a BookEquiv, with inverse tabulate and both inverse laws. Its first component is the length (lookup_length). The head index is inr star, and inl shifts a tail index. The formalization proves that under fin_below_equiv, the head index is 0 (fin_head_index) and inl is the successor (fin_shift_index). Thus x_i is the element at position i. lookup_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv (List A) (Table A) (lookup A).

For all book n ≥ 0, HLevel (n+2) X implies that the identity types of List X have HLevel (n+1). That is, List X is an n-type. The proof uses direct structural recursion on the two lists with the encode–decode codes (list_path_equiv). It does not use the tabulation of the printed proof.

The formal content of the argument is as follows. A proposition is finite iff it is decidable (finite_prop_iff_decidable). If it is finite, it holds iff its cardinality is 1 (proposition_cardinality_one). A decidable predicate on a finite type has a finite total space (finite_decidable_subset). The headline 'a subset of a finite set is not necessarily finite' is a metatheoretic remark and has no formal counterpart. No excluded-middle principle, or negation of it, is assumed. The formalization states the headline as an equivalence (subsets_finite_excluded_middle_equiv, module 284). Every subset (Prop-valued predicate) of every finite set is finite if and only if excluded middle holds. The forward direction is the remark's argument: a proposition p is a subset of 1, and a finite proposition is decidable.

For any decidable proposition-valued predicate on a merely finite type, both ∃ (as Mere Σ) and Π are decidable (finite_quantifiers). The proof uses induction on n for standard Fin n (fin_forall_decidable, fin_sigma_decidable). Then it eliminates the finiteness witness into the proposition, as the book hints.

The formalization has all three parts. First, finite dependent sums of finite types are finite (finite_sigma). Second, the cardinality formula Card(Σ_x F(x)) = Card(X)·Card(Y) holds for given fiber equivalences e(x) : F(x) ≃ Y. This is cardinality_equinumerous_sum, for any family of types F. Third, the arithmetical sum Σ_x f(x) (arithmetic_sum) is defined as the cardinality of Σ_x Fin(f x). The formalization also proves invariance under reindexing, the constant case, and the zero/successor equations for standard finite types. No enumeration is selected.

For every finite A and decidable equivalence relation R, the constructed image quotient A/R is finite. The proof selects representatives only for explicit Fin n. For arbitrary A, finiteness comes from elimination into a proposition. This uses decidable equality of the quotient (quotient_decidable_equality) and finite surjection targets (finite_surjection_target).

e_a : B(a) ≃ fst⁻¹(a) has the exact forward map b ↦ ((a,b), refl a) in the book fiber orientation. Its construction uses contract_away_map, as in the proof. The inverse law uses the typal contract_away_beta. projection_fiber_equiv is the native-orientation version. book_projection_inclusion_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of e_a = b ↦ ((a, b), refl a).

The formal statement is Σ(b:B) f⁻¹(b) ≃ A, with book fibers b = f(a) and the exact underlying map (b, a, p) ↦ a. It is the composite of the three printed steps (swap, contract away, projection). book_sum_of_fibers_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of e, (b, a, p) ↦ a.

preim : Σ(B : Type) (B → A) → (A → Type), (B, f) ↦ (a ↦ f⁻¹(a)), with book-oriented fibers, is a BookEquiv. The inverse sends C to (Σ_a C(a), fst). Both inverse laws use the constructed ua and its judgmental forward transport, as in the proof. The path-over step uses J with the typal transport computation at refl. The universe is the single native Type, so the footnote's same-universe condition is automatic. The exercise after lem:Prop-Set-pointed-families has a two-universe variant: families of U-small types versus maps in U′ with essentially U-small fibers. This variant is small_families_maps_equiv (module 193). The same-universe form for every model universe U and A : U is Σ_{B:U}(B → A) ≃ (A → U). This is universe_maps_families_equiv (module 284). Its map is preim by definition (universe_maps_families_map), and its inverse is C ↦ (Σ_a C(a), fst). small_families_maps_equiv is the two-universe statement of the unlabeled exercise at 4692, not this lemma. maps_families_equiv_book_map (module 289) states BookIsEquiv of preim.

The formal statement is Σ_{x:X} T(x) ≃ Σ_{y:Y} T(ptoe(p)(y)) for p : Y = X. Here ptoe is id_to_equiv, the path-to-equivalence map with a definition by J. It is equal to transport by id_to_equiv_transport.
The formal statement is (X → Σ(Y : Type) S(Y)) ≃ Σ(F : X → Type) Π(x:X) S(F x). It is an instance of type-theoretic choice (choice_equiv). The universe is the single native Type.

The formalization has all four displayed equivalences. These include the general S (structured_families_equiv) and its instances S = isProp, isSet and the identity (proposition_families_equiv, set_families_equiv, pointed_families_equiv). PointedTypes = Σ(A : Type) A is the book's U_*, and fibers are book fibers. The proof follows the book. It uses xca:sum-families, then pullback along the equivalence preim of lem:typefamiliesandfibrations (through ua), then reassociation. Narya efafad2 has a single universe Type : Type (levels are planned upstream). The statements are for U = Type.

The formalization has both parts. First, subtypes correspond to predicates through fibers (subtypes_injections_equiv). The inverse of this equivalence sends (S, i) to t ↦ i⁻¹(t). Module 21 proves it directly, not as an instance of lem:Prop-Set-pointed-families. Second, Inj(T) is a set for any type T (injections_into_set).

Let U : U′ be a nested pair of the model. Then the projection to the U-type is an equivalence (Σ_{A:U′} S(A)) ≃ U, with S(A) = Σ_{X:U} (A ≃ X) (essentially_small_types_equiv). This uses native Equiv, which is equivalent to the book form by essentially_small_book_equiv. For every A : U′, there is an equivalence (A → U) ≃ Σ_{B:U′} Σ_{f:B→A} Π_a S(f⁻¹(a)) (small_families_maps_equiv). B lies in U′ automatically (upper_small_of_small_fibers). The proof uses structured_families_equiv and univalence.

The formalization constructs all n-truncations for n = k − 1 ≥ −1. They are indexed by k : ℕ (an n-type has HLevel index k + 1). The construction is by recursion on k (truncation k A : TruncStructure k A). Level k = 0 is judgmentally the constructed propositional truncation Mere. Level k + 1 is literally the image of I_n : A → (A → NTypes k), x ↦ (y ↦ ‖x = y‖_n), with the image factor as unit (trunc_succ_image is refl). It is an (n+1)-type, because the type of n-types is an (n+1)-type (ntypes_level). The formalization proves the universal property (‖A‖_n → B) ≃ (A → B) for every n-type B and the literal precomposition map. The proof is as in the book and uses contractible types of extensions over the fibers of the surjective unit. eq:trunc-path-eq is trunc_path_equiv: the map ‖x = y‖_n → (|x| = |y|) that the universal property induces is an equivalence. Its generator (x = y) → (|x| = |y|) is transport of refl, not ap of the unit. The reason is that path induction on ap of the image unit raised Narya bug E0500. The two agree by path induction. The proof deviates from the book as follows. The inverse is the book's 'going backwards at |refl_y|'. That is, the decoding of a path p is the transport of |refl_y| backwards along p in the code family w ↦ w(y) (trunc_step_decode). The book leaves implicit the construction of the equivalence (|x| = |y|) ≃ Π_z (‖x = z‖_n ≃ ‖y = z‖_n) and the check of both composites. The proof does not build this equivalence. It shows that decoding is a left inverse of the induced map (truncation induction, which reduces to J on |r|). It also shows that decoding is injective. A path in the image is determined by its action on the code types (subtype paths, function extensionality, univalence). A family of maps ‖y = z‖_n → ‖x = z‖_n is determined by its value at |refl_y| (Yoneda and the universal property). An injective left inverse is a two-sided inverse. Thus the proof needs the chain of equivalences only as injectivity and never computes it on elements. Dependent elimination into families of n-types is trunc_induction_book. A computation rule, as an identification, is proved only for the variant trunc_ind (module 230, trunc_ind_beta). Level 1 is equivalent to the SetTrunc of module 43 and respects units up to identification (trunc_one_set_trunc_equiv, trunc_one_unit_compare). Both are images of the mere identity relation. Level 1 encodes propositions as HLevel 1, and SetTrunc encodes them as isProp. The recursor of SetTrunc computes judgmentally. But trunc_extend computes on units only up to trunc_extend_beta. The final resizing step is proved in the universe model. Let U be a universe that satisfies replacement. Then ‖A‖_n is essentially U-small for every essentially U-small A and every n ≥ −1 (trunc_essentially_small, trunc_small). The proof is by induction. It uses eq:trunc-path-eq for local smallness at units, the surjectivity of the unit, and replacement. Level −1 follows from the closure of U under truncation. The construction itself needs no resizing: NTypes k and the image live in the single native Type (Type : Type).

section_raw: Higher structure: stuff, structure, and properties}
note: This is an open-ended exercise. The formalization analyzes examples with the exact level of what is forgotten. The diagonal of a groupoid forgets at most structure. For FinSet, it forgets actual structure, not properties (finite_diagonal_not_injective). The map Cycles → Permutations forgets cyclicity, and it forgets at most properties. The map Permutations → Set forgets the permutation. It forgets at most structure, but not only properties (the fiber over Bool is Aut(Bool)). Two further examples have codomain Type, which is not a groupoid. Thus they are outside the exercise's 'maps between groupoids'. The map Set → Type forgets sethood, and it forgets at most properties. The map PointedTypes → Type forgets the point, and it does not forget at most structure. The reason is that the fiber over Set is not a set (pointed_types_forget_not_structure). No upper bound is claimed for this map (its fiber over Type is Type, which is not a groupoid). Module 284 treats maps between groupoids, as the exercise asks. Every map between groupoids forgets at most stuff (groupoid_map_one_truncated). Non-empty sets → Set forgets at most properties, and it does forget something (the fiber over the empty set is empty). Pointed sets → Set forgets at most structure, and not only properties. Set → 1 forgets stuff, and not only structure. Pointed groupoids → groupoids is a map between 2-types. The map that forgets the point forgets stuff and not only structure (pointed_groupoids_forget_stuff, pointed_groupoids_forget_not_structure).

section_raw: The circle and its universal property}
note: CircleSignature (module 05) is the circle as an interface. It is a type with base, loop and dependent induction for every family P : C → Type. Its computation rule is one identification (f(base), apd_f(loop)) = (a, l) of the whole boundary datum. Thus the book's judgmental f(base) ≡ a is an identification. This is a missing feature: Narya efafad2 has no HITs. Recursion is circle_rec, with the rule circle_rec_beta. The term constructed_circle (modules 220–223) inhabits the interface without postulates. It follows Bezem–Buchholtz–Grayson–Shulman. The carrier is the component Cyc_0 of (ℤ, succ) in Cycles. The base is (ℤ, succ), and the loop is its successor symmetry (circle_loop). Maps from (ℤ, succ) into a type with an automorphism are determined by the image of one point (int_maps_equiv). The version whose map is evaluation at 0 itself is int_maps_evaluation_equiv (module 284). This gives (Cyc_0 → A) ≃ Σ(a:A)(a = a) for every type A (circle_universal_equiv). Then it gives dependent induction (circle_induction_from_recursion). The choice of the loop generator has no effect, because all chapter-3 results are stated for an arbitrary circle. The book postulates "S¹ : U". The formalization proves it for every model universe U that satisfies replacement (pri:replacement). The cycles with a U-small carrier form a locally U-small type (small_carrier_cycles_locally_small). Its component at (ℤ, succ) is Cyc_0. Thus the constructed circle is essentially U-small (constructed_circle_essentially_small). Hence it is an element of U (constructed_circle_small, constructed_circle_code, small_circle_signature). Also, every circle is essentially U-small (circle_carrier_essentially_small). The only concrete model universe is the universe of all types (total_constructed_circle_essentially_small). Induction over all families P : C → Type uses Narya's single universe Type : Type. The formalization also gives freeness with the evaluation map: int_maps_evaluation_equiv (module 284) is an equivalence (Z, succ) → (Y, F) ≃ Y. By definition, its map is evaluation at 0 (int_maps_evaluation_map). It is the chain of int_maps_equiv with an explicit reindexing of sums (sigma_reindex_equiv). The map of int_maps_equiv itself is not definitionally evaluation at 0.
